analysis.title: CIO Notebook: Fed Holds Rates Steady, Cites the Need for More Information
key_insights: The FOMC held the fed funds target rate at 3.75% to 4.00%, as expected. Beth Hammack and Lisa Cook both dissented, preferring a 25-basis point hike.
Neuberger views the tone as more dovish than September. A December hike remains highly probable, while 2027 pricing implies slightly lower odds of further hikes.

The statement described economic activity as growing at a "strong" pace, versus "solid" last month. It added that "the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance" needed to reach the 2% inflation target.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh cited geopolitical uncertainty, strong GDP led by consumer spending and accelerating business investment, and a labor market with lower unemployment and claims. He cited evidence of tightening financial conditions after September's hike, including greater discernment in capital allocation.

Warsh described a "new monetary medicine": a doubling down on the 2% target, a responsibility to deliver it apart from exogenous factors, and a new framework for how policy and its transmission should operate. He framed the Fed's role as to "interrogate reality", with emphasis on price stability through clear objectives rather than a fixed date or single data point.

The FOMC will keep eight meetings a year, but in 2027 and 2028 one and two meetings respectively will be strategic discussions with no policy action or statement. Neuberger found it somewhat surprising that the schedule was released ahead of the findings of the five new task forces.

Neuberger sees the period through the December meeting as information-rich and important for the pace of hikes. Repeated references to tightening financial conditions and correlations may indicate greater Fed reliance on real-time economic and market data.
Guidance was hard to glean and the Fed's reaction function appears to be a work in progress, which could mean greater short-term volatility.
Stocks were modestly higher and short-term yields drifted lower after the meeting.

September PCE is released the next day and October non-farm payrolls follow the next Friday. Anthropic's S-1 filing and continued equity and debt issuance for AI buildout could tighten conditions and liquidity and weigh on the narrative into year-end.

Neuberger's positioning: cut U.S. small-mid cap and emerging market equity, added to U.S. large cap and Japan, trimmed duration, kept credit near target, added to commodities, and held private equity and private debt at target.
